title: Epidural Stimulation–Enabled Motor Recovery in Complete Thoracic Spinal Cord Injury Using a 32-Contact Electrode Array: A Case Series
content: Complete thoracic spinal cord injury (SCI) causes severe motor and sensory impairment. Epidural electrical stimulation (EES) may facilitate activation of spinal motor networks, although clinical experience with 32-contact electrode arrays remains limited. This prospective case series evaluated intraoperative electromyography (EMG)-guided electrode placement, postoperative stimulation programming, and functional outcomes in four participants (two males and two females, aged 18–42 years) with thoracic SCI classified as AIS A at baseline. Participants underwent implantation of a 32-contact epidural array targeting the lumbosacral enlargement at T11–T12, followed by eight weeks of individualized EES programming and neurorehabilitation. Intraoperative EMG mapping guided electrode positioning and demonstrated preferential recruitment of proximal muscles by rostral contacts and distal muscles by caudal contacts, with mixed responses from intermediate contacts. Asymmetric responses in two participants were addressed through lead repositioning. After eight weeks, mean Lower Extremity Motor Score increased from 0 to 18.1 ± 1.5; mean light-touch score increased from 51.6 ± 1.0 to 62.1 ± 1.0, and mean pin-prick score increased from 52.2 ± 1.0 to 61.8 ± 1.0. Three participants achieved a Modified Ashworth Scale score of 0, while one regained voluntary anal contraction and deep anal pressure and was reclassified as AIS C. All participants stood for 30–45 minutes using a walker and demonstrated stepping with minimal assistance. These findings support the feasibility of physiology-guided 32-contact EES combined with rehabilitation, without establishing comparative efficacy over lower-density arrays. Larger controlled studies are needed to establish safety and durability.
